seo_title: Cost of Living in Jakarta 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Jakarta per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Indonesia's capital and the country's business hub: a 30-day visa on arrival, low prices and year-round tropics. The downsides are the famous traffic jams, the humidity and the air quality of a megacity.
pros: Low prices for housing and food
A business hub with work and services
cons: High humidity and air quality issues
Few beaches within the city itself
A language barrier outside the business centre

visa_steps.title: Visa on arrival
visa_steps.description: Russian citizens can get a visa on arrival (VOA) for 30 days, with renewal.

visa_steps.title: Renting a home
visa_steps.description: Apartments are rented by the month; the SCBD and Menteng districts are popular.

visa_steps.title: Connectivity and money
visa_steps.description: A local SIM card is cheap; you'll need rupiah in cash and a card from a foreign bank.

visa_steps.title: Visa extension
visa_steps.description: The VOA can be extended once at the immigration office.

visa_steps.title: Long-term stay
visa_steps.description: For living there longer, people consider KITAS visas (work or retirement).

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Jakarta?
faq.answer: Yes, a visa on arrival (VOA) for 30 days with the option to extend.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Jakarta?
faq.answer: Affordable: cheaper than many Asian capitals, especially food. The exact budget is in the calculator above.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Jakarta?
faq.answer: Indonesian; English is widely used in business circles and in tourism.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Jakarta?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You'll need rupiah in cash and a card from a foreign bank.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Jakarta?
faq.answer: Tropical: hot and humid year-round, with a pronounced rainy season.

faq.question: How does Jakarta differ from Bali?
faq.answer: Jakarta is a business megacity without beaches; Bali is a resort island. Many choose Bali for living and Jakarta for work.

reviews.text: Jakarta is a working megacity: cheap, warm, with infrastructure. The downside is the hellish traffic and the air — on weekends I escape to the sea.
It's not a resort city, but it's convenient for work and life, and the prices are pleasing. English is enough in business circles, but the traffic really wears you out.
